title: Councillor pay decision and water allocation policy
subtitle: Winter maintenance review, internal audit plan, parking strategy scope and a closed-session land item on Neeve Street
overview: Council held the mayor's salary at the current rate for the 2026-2030 term, with yearly increases tied to the non-union employee economic increase {{vote:m8}}. It did not approve the staff proposal for a large councillor raise. A motion to raise the councillor salary to $55,000 was sent to the March 31 Council meeting, with staff to prepare a memo with more information {{vote:m14}}. Council also asked for comparison with single-tier municipalities of 130,000 to 500,000 people {{vote:m15}}, and directed a ward boundary and council composition review before the 2030 election {{vote:m9}}.

Council approved the Internal Audit Work Plan 2026-2028 and directed staff to report on winter control and maintenance service levels, including costs and community engagement {{vote:m4}}. It also approved a Water and Wastewater Servicing Allocation Policy and by-law, giving the Deputy CAO of Infrastructure, Development and Environment authority to administer it {{vote:m16}}. The City-Wide Parking Strategy scope of work was approved on consent {{vote:m3}}.
In closed session on the Neeve Street parking lot, Council received information, then later gave direction to staff. No details were released.

decisions.detail: The mayor's salary stays at the 2026 rate for the 2026-2030 term, with annual increases equal to the non-union municipal employee economic increase {{vote:m8}}.
A motion to raise the councillor salary to $55,000 was referred to the March 31 Council meeting, with staff working with the Corporate Services chair on a memo {{vote:m14}}.
The City Clerk is directed to review ward boundaries and council composition, including pay and benefits for elected officials, before the 2030 election, subject to 2028 budget funding {{vote:m9}}.
Council asked that councillor pay be reviewed against single-tier Ontario municipalities with populations between 130,000 and 500,000 {{vote:m15}}.

decisions.item: Internal audit plan and winter maintenance
decisions.detail: Council approved the 2026-2028 audit work plan and directed staff to report back on winter control service levels, with financial analysis and community engagement {{vote:m4}}.
Council approved the allocation policy and by-law and delegated administration to the Deputy CAO of Infrastructure, Development and Environment {{vote:m16}}.
The scope of work for the City-Wide Parking Strategy terms of reference was approved on the consent report {{vote:m3}}.

debate: On winter maintenance, staff said the operational review would start after a value-for-money audit reports in September, with results ready around January 2027 for the next term of Council. Staff said community engagement would follow once there was something concrete to comment on.
Staff said removing winter on-street parking would cost roughly $350,000 in revenue and could also hinder snow clearing. They said this question is part of the parking strategy.

A delegate urged Council to accept the staff pay recommendation. The delegate said zero growth undervalues the role and makes it harder to attract a diverse range of candidates. Some councillors agreed that pay affects who can serve.

Other councillors questioned the comparator list, noting it mixes single-tier, upper-tier and lower-tier municipalities. One said salaries are not frozen because they rise with the annual economic increase, and suggested extra pay for committee chairs instead. Several objected to choosing a $55,000 figure without staff analysis, while one objected to asking staff to justify a number Council had chosen.

On water allocation, a delegate supported the use-it-or-lose-it approach and asked for annual public reporting on extensions requested, granted and declined. Staff said reporting would go through the growth management monitoring report, and exemption detail would likely appear in later years.
